user.title: Yeelight Quota Guard
user.description: To restart a bulb from Home Assistant, the guard needs each bulb's miIO token. Get them all at once from your Xiaomi account, or type them one by one.

cloud.title: Xiaomi account
cloud.description: The account the bulbs were added with in Mi Home or the Yeelight app. The password is used only for this request and is not saved.

data_description.country: The region chosen in the Mi Home app. Europe is usually Germany.

cloud_done.title: Bulbs to guard

manual.title: Token by hand
manual.description: Pick the bulb and paste its 32-character miIO token. The bulb is asked straight away, so a wrong token is caught here.

cloud_captcha.title: Xiaomi captcha
cloud_captcha.description:
Xiaomi wants to make sure a person is signing in. Type the characters in the picture.

![captcha]({image})

cloud_code.title: Xiaomi verification code
cloud_code.description: Xiaomi has sent a code to {address}. Type it here. It expires in a few minutes.

abort.no_yeelight: Set up your bulbs with Home Assistant's Yeelight integration first: the guard watches the bulbs that integration knows.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration possible.

menu_options.manual: Add or replace a token by hand
menu_options.cloud: Fetch tokens again from my Xiaomi account

data.prevent_after_days: Restart after this many days powered on
data.only_when_off: Only while the light is off

data_description.repair: A bulb past 49.7 days is restarted at once, at any hour: it no longer obeys Home Assistant anyway. So is a younger one Home Assistant has asked to power cycle for two checks in a row while it stays silent on the LAN.
data_description.prevent: Bulbs close to the limit are restarted inside the quiet window.
data_description.prevent_after_days: The lock comes at 49.7 days. 45 leaves several nights to find the light off.
data_description.only_when_off: A restart keeps the light as it was, but this avoids touching a light someone is using.
